rv.q: You will be sobbing before the evening is over, just as surely as you will jump to your feet cheering and applauding wildly at its triumphant end.
In the process, Sherman gives us a heroic tragedy of heartbreaking simplicity.

cn.t: Dukakis delivers a dazzling, gut-wrenching performance in Sherman's one-woman play about an 80-year-old Holocaust survivor, though the staging remains static. Critics praise her powerful embodiment of 20th-century history.

vs.sum: The Lyceum Theatre offers good sightlines and a charming Beaux Arts ambiance, but suffers from cramped seating and small restrooms. Ideal for intimate dramas, but patrons should be prepared for less comfort during their visit.

acc.note: 4 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. No elevator. Infrared devices available.
